# googleworkspace_chrome_resolved_policies (Data Source)

Resolved Chrome Policies data source in the Terraform Googleworkspace provider. It reads the effective (resolved) values of the Chrome policies for an org unit, also the values that the org unit inherits from a parent org unit. A policy that is not set in the org unit or in a parent org unit is not in the result, or is in the result with an empty `source_org_unit_id` (the default value for the customer). Use it in a `check` block to verify a policy value or that a policy is not set. The data source uses the `policies:resolve`, `policySchemas.get`, and `policySchemas.list` methods, which need the `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/chrome.management.policy` client scope (in the default scopes) or the `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/chrome.management.policy.readonly` client scope.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Copyright (c) HashiCorp, Inc.
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MPL-2.0

# The effective values of the chrome.users.* policies for an org unit, also the values that it inherits.
data "googleworkspace_chrome_resolved_policies" "users" {
  org_unit_id          = "id:01ab2c3d4efg56h"
  policy_schema_filter = "chrome.users.*"
}

locals {
  resolved_users = {
    for p in data.googleworkspace_chrome_resolved_policies.users.resolved_policies :
    p.schema_name => p
    if length(p.additional_target_keys) == 0
  }
}

# Assert a value: incognito mode is unavailable.
# Enum value names have a prefix (<PREFIX>_ENUM_<VALUE>). Confirm the full name with the enum_fields attribute of
# googleworkspace_chrome_policy_schema instead of guessing the prefix.
data "googleworkspace_chrome_policy_schema" "incognito" {
  schema_name = "chrome.users.IncognitoMode"
}

locals {
  # null if the schema has no such value, so that a schema change fails the check, not the plan.
  incognito_unavailable = try(one(flatten([
    for f in data.googleworkspace_chrome_policy_schema.incognito.enum_fields : [
      for v in f.values : v.value if endswith(v.value, "_UNAVAILABLE")
    ] if f.field == "incognitoModeAvailability"
  ])), null)
}

check "incognito_mode_unavailable" {
  assert {
    # The API can omit a field at its default value, so read it with try() or lookup() and compare decoded values.
    condition = local.incognito_unavailable != null && try(
      jsondecode(local.resolved_users["chrome.users.IncognitoMode"].schema_values["incognitoModeAvailability"]),
      null,
    ) == local.incognito_unavailable
    error_message = "chrome.users.IncognitoMode must make incognito mode unavailable."
  }
}

# Assert that a policy is not set in the org unit or in a parent org unit. The result can still have the policy with
# the default value for the customer: then source_org_unit_id is empty.
# A read error of a data source in a check block is a warning, not an error, as is a failed assertion.
check "hsts_bypass_list_not_set" {
  data "googleworkspace_chrome_resolved_policies" "hsts" {
    org_unit_id          = "id:01ab2c3d4efg56h"
    policy_schema_filter = "chrome.users.HstsPolicyBypassList"
  }

  assert {
    condition = alltrue([
      for p in data.googleworkspace_chrome_resolved_policies.hsts.resolved_policies : p.source_org_unit_id == ""
    ])
    error_message = "chrome.users.HstsPolicyBypassList must not be set."
  }
}

# The policies that the org unit inherits, and the org unit that sets each one.
output "inherited_policies" {
  value = {
    for name, p in local.resolved_users : name => p.source_org_unit_id
    if p.inherited
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `org_unit_id` (String) The ID of the org unit for which the policies are resolved, not its path. The `id:` prefix is optional.
- `policy_schema_filter` (String) The schema name of one policy (for example `chrome.users.PasswordManager`), or a filter with a wildcard in the leaf part of the name (for example `chrome.users.*` or `chrome.users.apps.*`). A wildcard in the namespace (for example `chrome.*`) is not valid.

### Optional

- `additional_target_keys` (Map of String) Additional target keys for policies that need them, for example `app_id` for `chrome.users.apps.*` policies. The `additional_target_key_names` attribute of `googleworkspace_chrome_policy_schema` gives the key names.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `resolved_policies` (List of Object) The resolved policies, in the order that the API returns them. Each element has these attributes: `schema_name`; `value`, the resolved value as a JSON object of the schema fields in canonical form (each value has the type of its schema field, for example integers are numbers, not strings); `schema_values`, each field value JSON encoded in the same canonical form; `source_org_unit_id`, the ID (without the `id:` prefix) of the org unit in which the policy is set, empty if the API returns no source (the value is the default value for the customer); `inherited`, true if the policy is not set in `org_unit_id` itself; and `additional_target_keys`, for example the `app_id` of an app policy. The API can omit a field that has its default value, so a field can be absent from `value` and `schema_values`. Read a field with `lookup(p.schema_values, "field", null)` or `try(jsondecode(p.value).field, null)`, and compare decoded values (`jsondecode`), not JSON strings. If a value cannot be converted (for example, the schema cannot be read or does not describe a field), `value` and `schema_values` have the raw API value of that policy, with a warning. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--resolved_policies))
